text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped 2.8% over the past two trading days, with today's modest gain of 0.52% continuing a sharp reversal that started October 1st. The driver appears to be oil prices: crude spiked to $96.16 domestically and $113.96 globally, a meaningful move that benefits refiners' margins. Refineries are running at 92.5% capacity, near optimal levels, which means MPC can convert that higher-priced crude into fuel products more efficiently when margins widen—and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East (tanker strikes near Iran, U.S. military repositioning) are keeping oil elevated and supplies tight.

The G7's plan to release 100 million barrels of diesel reserves over four months was announced October 2nd and initially pressured prices downward, but the offsetting supply concerns from regional conflicts appear to have won out. With inventories still moderate (gasoline and diesel/heating oil storage both in normal ranges), the refining sector is positioned to profit from the price structure that's emerged.
